description: Earth Trend Detectives is a solo team led by Abdullah Bin Haseeb, participating in the Islamabad Local Event for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our challenge is "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" — exploring Earth system trends using NASA data.
summary: An interactive dashboard that turns 146 years of NASA temperature data into a clear, statistically certain answer: Earth has warmed by +1.26 °C since 1880, and the warming is now happening 5.5× faster than it did in the first century of the record.
details: Earth Trend Detective is a single-page, no-server dashboard built on one authoritative NASA dataset (GISS GISTEMP v4) that answers the challenge's four questions with real, computed numbers: an interactive annual chart (1880–2025) with the least-squares trend line; a decade-average bar chart; a decade × month heatmap proving warming in every month of the year; a plain-language answers section; and a 72-second narrated demo video. Method: parsed the GISTEMP v4 CSV with Python (pandas, treating missing values as missing); linear trend by ordinary least-squares regression on annual means with slope per decade, R² and p-value (SciPy); acceleration from separate regressions for 1880–1980 and 1981–2025. Key findings: +1.26 °C total warming (1880–1909 mean −0.25 °C to 2015–2025 mean +1.00 °C); +0.08 °C/decade trend 1880–2025, p = 4.95×10⁻⁴⁷, R² = 0.76; +0.21 °C/decade since 1981 vs +0.04 °C/decade before — 5.5× faster; warmest year 2024 (+1.28 °C); all 10 warmest years are 2015 or later.
